headline: High: Continue’s filesystem/MCP access can collide with Opik’s REST/API workflows, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so if Opik outputs are placed in shared files or MCP-fed content, Continue may ingest attacker-controlled text as instructions. Opik exposes a REST API and broad egress, but its profile does not show direct ingestion of Continue outputs. The shared filesystem bridge makes the pathway plausible, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF Opik output is written into a workspace file or MCP-fed artifact that Continue reads
IF Continue is configured to treat file content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from workspace files
Route Opik outputs to a separate non-workspace directory
Require explicit human review before MCP-fed content is acted on
Add provenance tags to Opik-generated artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization at the orchestrator boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; Opik exposes REST API access and broad egress. If they share a workspace or the same data is copied into Opik requests, sensitive code or buffers can leave the local environment. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Continue buffers or workspace files are forwarded into Opik REST requests
IF both agents are run against the same shared project directory
mitigations: Keep Opik on redacted samples only
Separate workspaces per agent
Block outbound requests containing source-code patterns
Review API payloads before send
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on the API boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write and broad egress, while Opik has REST API access and broad egress. Even without explicit write overlap in Opik, both can mutate shared external resources if pointed at the same project or service, creating coordination risk. Because Opik’s writable surfaces are not documented, I cannot justify high severity and must escalate uncertainty conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents target the same shared filesystem or remote API resource
IF Continue writes files that Opik also reads or evaluates
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Avoid concurrent writes to the same remote resource
Serialize access with a simple operator checklist
Use read-only mounts for Opik inputs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or edits from workspace context, and Opik can consume results through REST/API workflows. If Opik treats Continue’s output as authoritative, errors can propagate into downstream evaluation or actions. The profiles do not show direct action-taking authority for Opik, so this is a default-path inference rather than a documented high-risk chain.
conditions: IF Opik ingests Continue-generated text without verification
IF Continue output is used as a source of truth for Opik evaluation or routing
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Opik consumes Continue output
Require citations or diffs for any generated claims
Limit Continue output to suggestions, not commands
Manually spot-check a sample of handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit regulated-data handling, residency, or retention mismatch. Continue touches source code and editor buffers; Opik’s touched data classes are empty, so there is no documented compliance breach pathway beyond ordinary operational caution. I do not cite Opik-specific residency claims because none are present.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Continue buffers
IF Opik is configured to store or export that regulated data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Review retention settings before use
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Document data-class boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data
